title: Strict logarithmic Jacobian criterion
statement:
Let $S,X,Y$ be locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be log smooth [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], and let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of log schemes with $f=gh$. Assume $h$ is strict, meaning that its source log structure is the associated log structure of the inverse image of the target log structure with its induced map to $\mathcal O_X$ [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, put $\bar y=h\bar x$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$ and $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Use the logarithmic differential modules of [def-per-log-differential-stalk] and their natural comparison of [def-per-log-cotangent-comparison]. If the induced $k$-linear map
$$k\otimes_B\omega_{g,\bar y}\longrightarrow k\otimes_A\omega_{f,\bar x}$$
is injective, then the underlying scheme morphism $h$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $\bar x$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. No regularity of the underlying schemes or perfection of any residue field is assumed. Tensor products and scalar extension have their usual module meanings [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138: strictness and the logarithmic Jacobian criterion explicitly attributed to Kato 1988 Proposition 3.12. The general criterion in Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, Proposition 3.12 is WANTED locally. No Stacks tag states the logarithmic assertion.

proof.text: Write $E=h^*\omega_g$, $F=\omega_f$, with $u:E\to F$ defined by $da\mapsto d(h^*a)$ and $d\log m\mapsto d\log h^\flat m$. The chart deformation calculus gives finite locally free logarithmic differential sheaves, with these properties preserved by strict etale localization. Choose a pointed strict etale neighbourhood $e:U\to X$, and then an affine open in it, on which $E$ and $F$ have finite bases. Its geometric stalks identify with the given stalks: a pointed etale neighbourhood is cofinal among pointed etale neighbourhoods. The relations defining the differential stalk and the comparison identify the fibre of $u$ with the map in the hypothesis. If $p$ is the point of $U$ under the chosen geometric point, the matrix of $u$ over $\kappa(p)$ therefore has independent columns: a nonzero relation over $\kappa(p)$ would remain a nonzero relation over its field extension $k$. Apply the finite-free residue-localization lemma to this matrix over $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. After a principal shrinking containing $p$, there is a left inverse $r:F|_U\to E|_U$, and $C=\operatorname{coker}(u|_U)$ is free of finite rank $d$. Thus $ru=1$ and $F|_U=u(E|_U)\oplus\ker r$, with $\ker r\simeq C$. All these sheaf identities follow from the matrix identities, so remain true after pullback. Replace $f,h$ by their composites with $e$ during the lifting argument.

proof.text: The underlying $h:U\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation. The chart deformation calculus gives this for $U\to S$ and $Y\to S$. For each point choose compatible affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$, $\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset U$ with $h(\operatorname{Spec}A')\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine-open finite-presentation lemma says that $B$ and $A'$ are finitely presented over $R$. In particular $B$ is of finite type over $R$, so the intermediate-algebra finite-presentation lemma applied to $R\to B\to A'$ says that $A'$ is finitely presented over $B$. These opens cover $U$.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary first order thickening of affine schemes $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, with ideal $\mathcal I$, and maps $a_0:T_0\to U$, $b:T\to Y$ satisfying $ha_0=bi$. Give $T$ the pulled-back log structure $b^*M_Y$ and $T_0$ its pullback. These are fine log structures even when the test schemes are not Noetherian: etale locally on $Y$ choose a finite integral chart $P$ and use on its pullbacks the associated chart log structure of the fine-chart logification lemma. That lemma supplies its universal property and says that reduction modulo $\mathcal I$ is strict. The local constructions agree because their maps are uniquely determined by the inverse-image log sheaf and the units. Since $h$ is strict, $a_0$ has the canonical log map over $Y$: its log pullback is $(ha_0)^*M_Y=(bi)^*M_Y$. The same statement holds for any scheme lift over $Y$. Conversely a log lift over $Y$ gives such a scheme lift. Apply the chart deformation calculus to $U\to S$. It supplies log lifts $a:T\to U$ over $S$ on an etale cover of $T$. This uses only fine test structures, not saturation or Noetherianity of $T$.

proof.text: On any member of this cover, $ha$ and $b$ are log lifts over $S$ of the same map on $T_0$. By the torsor clause of the chart deformation calculus there is a unique $\delta:(ha_0)^*\omega_g\to\mathcal I$ with sign convention $ha=b+\delta$. Put $\epsilon=-\delta\circ a_0^*r:a_0^*\omega_f\to\mathcal I$ and let $a'=a+\epsilon$ under the torsor action for $U/S$. On a function $v$ of $Y$ the change in $(ha)^\sharp(v)$ is $\epsilon(dh^*v)$, and on a log section $m$ it is multiplication by $1+\epsilon(d\log h^\flat m)$. Thus $ha'-ha=\epsilon\circ a_0^*u=-\delta$, because $ru=1$. The actions add since $(1+s)(1+t)=1+s+t$ for $s,t\in\mathcal I$. Therefore $ha'=b$ on both functions and log sections, and $a'|_{T_0}=a_0$. We have produced ordinary lifts over $Y$ etale locally on every test $T$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal L$ on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be the sheaf of ordinary lifts of this fixed square: on $v:V\to T$ it consists of maps $c:V\to U$ with $hc=bv$ and $c|_{V\times_TT_0}=a_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}$. It is a sheaf by the representable-presheaf sheaf theorem applied to $U\times_Y T$ over $T$; the restriction equality is local on the etale cover of $V\times_TT_0$. By Step 4 it is locally nonempty. Through strictness these are exactly the log lifts over $Y$. If $c,c'$ are two, the logarithmic torsor calculus over $S$ gives their unique difference $\eta:a_0^*F\to\mathcal I$. Their composites to $Y$ agree if and only if $\eta\circ a_0^*u=0$: this is checked on $dv$ and $d\log m$ by the action formulas. Hence differences factor uniquely through $a_0^*C$. Conversely every map $a_0^*C\to\mathcal I$ acts on $c$ and keeps $hc=bv$. These identifications commute with restriction because they are specified on the differential generators. Consequently $\mathcal L$ is a torsor under $\mathcal H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(a_0^*C,\mathcal I)$, viewed on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with scalars through $\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_{T_0}$. The free basis of $C$ identifies $\mathcal H$ with the etale sheaf associated to $\mathcal I^{\oplus d}$ on $T$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2 proof, printed p.138 (PDF p.144), strict logarithmic Jacobian argument; agent expansion using infinitesimal log lifts.

proof.text: The ideal $\mathcal I$ of a first order thickening is quasi-coherent. Since $T=\operatorname{Spec}D$ is affine, write $\mathcal I=\widetilde J$ for its defining ideal $J\subset D$. Then $\mathcal I^{\oplus d}=\widetilde{J^{\oplus d}}$: on each principal open $D(s)$ both modules have sections $(J_s)^{\oplus d}=(J^{\oplus d})_s$, by sending each coordinate fraction to a common denominator. Thus this finite direct sum is quasi-coherent, including $d=0$. Apply affine etale quasi-coherent vanishing to obtain $H^1(T_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathcal H)=0$. The torsor--$H^1$ classification sends the trivial torsor to zero, so the torsor $\mathcal L$ is trivial and has a global section (the image of zero in a trivialization). This section is the required scheme lift $T\to U$ over $Y$. As the affine square was arbitrary, $h:U\to Y$ is formally smooth.

source.place: Tag 03P2, theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent, affine vanishing; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; the torsor method in more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth.

proof.text: Together with Step 2, formal smoothness proves that $h:U\to Y$ is smooth by the definition of smooth morphisms. Apply the pointwise etale-source locality theorem to $e:U\to X$ at the chosen lift of $\bar x$. It says that the original $h:X\to Y$ is smooth at its image. By its stated meaning of smooth at a point, $h$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $\bar x$. The proof used no regularity of any underlying scheme and no perfection of any residue field.

theorem smooth_near_of_strict_logCotangent_injective
    {S X Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}}
    (f : EtaleLogHom X S) (g : EtaleLogHom Y S) (h : EtaleLogHom X Y)
    (hover : h.CompEq g f) (hf : f.IsLogSmooth) (hg : g.IsLogSmooth)
    (hstrict : h.IsStrict) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) (hinj : IsLogCotangentInjective f g h t) :
    ∃ U : X.scheme.Opens,
      (Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField Ω X.scheme t).1 ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ h.base)
